newsitem.title: USA: Is it art? Artist's opus closes Florida street.
newsitem.headline: Is it art? Artist's opus closes Florida street.

text.p: Police in Florida's capital were debating the meaning of art on Tuesday, a day after they closed a busy street for hours when they were alerted to an artist's creation that looked like a pipe bomb.

The device, four small pipes wrapped with electrical wire and topped with a small white plastic clock, was sitting in the storefront studio of Florida State University professor Paul Rutkovsky when it was spotted by Jeff Fleetwood, a city worker who had checked the buildings meter on Monday morning.
"I didn't really panic. I was like, whoa, it looks too real," Fleetwood told the Tallahassee Democrat. "I saw it sitting on the table and called 911."

Operators at the emergency number alerted police and sheriff's deputies, who evacuated and closed off the busy stretch of West Gaines Street for two hours before Rutkovsky got in touch with the bomb squad and told them the device was actually a decade-old work of art.
He said the artwork, called, "The Mail Art Liberation Organisation," had been in his studio since 1986, when it was part of an art show that his wife had curated.

Sgt. Jack Adkins, who led the bomb squad to the site, told the newspaper he was not surprised at getting a false alarm call. But he said he did not necessarily agree about the object's creative merit.
"I can't say we've ever dealt with a work of art, and obviously, in my profession, this is not a work of art," he said.
He took the sculpture away in the bomb squad's van to be impounded.
